# Checkpoint H — 1974 Straube evidence and correction to the 1985 interpretation

Date: 2026-09-12
Prepared outside Claude's restricted-web environment.

## Executive result

A WELT article published 25 Jan 2022 carries a Weltzeituhr photograph explicitly captioned:

> `Erinnerungsfoto 1974 auf dem Berliner Alexanderplatz`

and credits it to:

> `pa/akg-images/Straube`

Source page:
https://www.welt.de/reise/deutschland/article236437495/Urlaub-in-der-DDR-Ein-Museum-sucht-Erinnerungen-zu-Reise-Utensilien.html

Direct image URL surfaced by the page:
https://img.welt.de/img/reise/mobile236440269/8267932157-ci3x2l-w1200/Berlin-Alexanderplatz-Weltzeituhr-Foto-Berlin-Alexanderplatz.jpg

The image visibly shows the CET/UTC+1 lower band already containing at least **KOPENHAGEN** and **WIEN** in 1974.

This directly conflicts with a literal reading of the 2019 Tagesspiegel sentence:

> `Schon bei der ersten großen Wartung 1985 wurde aus gegebenem Anlass Athen nachgraviert, aber auch Kopenhagen, Wien und Rom.`

Tagesspiegel source:
https://www.tagesspiegel.de/berlin/die-weltzeituhr-kennt-jeder-niemand-ihren-erfinder-6541270.html

Therefore the 1985 sentence must NOT be used as proof that Kopenhagen/Wien first appeared in 1985. At minimum, for those two names, the visual 1974 evidence falsifies that interpretation.

Possible explanations include:

- `nachgraviert` described re-engraving / renewal during maintenance rather than first introduction;
- the retrospective article compressed several different maintenance actions;
- one of the later accounts is simply inaccurate.

Do not choose among these without further evidence.

## Consequence for the disputed Straube UTC+1 photograph

The previously used WELT image from article 217168174 is a **different Straube photograph**, credited the same way (`pa/akg-images/Straube`) and captioned only `Mitte der 70er-Jahre`.

Source page:
https://www.welt.de/reise/deutschland/article217168174/DDR-als-Urlaubsland-Wie-alte-Reisefuehrer-das-Land-zeigen.html

Direct image:
https://img.welt.de/img/reise/mobile217168152/1920313707-coriginal-w1200/Berlin-Alexanderplatz-Weltzeituhr-Foto.jpg

The new 1974 image does **not** prove that exact photograph was taken in 1974, but it materially strengthens the credibility of WELT's mid-1970s dating and removes the earlier argument that visible KOPENHAGEN/WIEN forced a post-1985 date.

The exact Source-3 shoot date remains unresolved unless the akg/picture-alliance catalogue record for that specific frame is recovered.

## Independent archive metadata that may help

Picture Alliance's public Weltzeituhr webseries exposes multiple archive-dated pre-1997 images, including:

- 22.05.1973 — IDs `102505875`, `102505844`, `102506000`
- 01.01.1982 — ID `15638904`
- 04.11.1989 — IDs `16008401`, `16008415`
- 05.08.1991 — ID `7728036`

Public webseries:
https://www.picture-alliance.com/webseries/weltzeituhr-in-berlin-w194131

These are useful as dated acquisition targets even where the image host itself is blocked.

## Evidence grading

- WELT 1974 date/caption + Straube credit: SOURCE-PUBLISHED, HIGH confidence as metadata.
- KOPENHAGEN and WIEN visible in that 1974 photograph: EXTERNAL-AGENT VISUAL TRANSCRIPTION, HIGH confidence.
- Claim that they were first added in 1985: CONTRADICTED by the 1974 photograph.
- Exact date of the other Straube UTC+1 photograph (image `1920313707`): still UNKNOWN beyond WELT's `mid-1970s` caption.

## Impact on Tier 1

This correction removes the internal date contradiction that arose solely from interpreting the 1985 Tagesspiegel sentence as a first-addition claim.

It does **not** by itself prove the complete CET face was unchanged through 1988–89, so Tier 1 should remain blocked until target-window attestation or another principled stability argument is established.

EXP-024 should remain frozen unless the existing Tier-1 rule is genuinely satisfied.
